children: May Mobility is going public, having inked a business-combination agreement with special purpose acquisition company ACP Holdings.

The deal, which implies a pro forma enterprise value of about $1.4 billion, will position May Mobility as the first pure-play, autonomous ride-hailing technology company to be publicly traded in the U.S., the companies said Wednesday.

Upon closing, expected by year-end, the combined company will operate as May Mobility and list on the Nasdaq under the ticker MAY. The business combination transaction is expected to deliver gross proceeds of up to $337 million.

May Mobility currently operates in three U.S. locations. The company previously partnered with Lyft to launch commercial operations in Atlanta, and it additionally offers autonomous ride services in Eden Prairie, Minn., as well as Grand Rapids, Minn.
In the coming months, May Mobility will partner with Uber to launch commercial operations in Arlington, Texas, it added.

May Mobility said it has completed more than 550,000 commercial autonomous rides. The company has pioneered an asset-light, partnership first approach to deploy physical artificial intelligence in autonomous ride-hailing applications, a move the company said differentiates it from other asset-heavy AV fleet operators.

"By partnering with the best companies in the world, we can give people a smarter way to move through their cities, at a scale none of us could reach alone," said Edwin Olson, CEO and founder of May Mobility.

May Mobility said its autonomous technology architecture is capable of navigating diverse driving environments safely and built to scale efficiently. Under the partnerships, fleet operating partners assume full responsibility of vehicle ownership, depot operations and maintenance costs.
May Mobility generated about $10 million in revenue in 2025, and the company has raised roughly $445 million from investors and corporate partners since its inception in 2017.

"May Mobility has demonstrated meaningful commercial traction, validation of technology and a robust ecosystem of strategic partners," said Andrew Mallozzi, chief executive of ACP Holdings. "We are pleased to support the company's next phase of growth through this transaction."
